title: Bitcoin's volatility has plunged, but extreme price swings are more frequent than in 2018
summary: Title: Bitcoin's falling volatility hides a risk that Wall Street models may miss URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/09/bitcoin-s-volatility-has-plunged-but-extreme-price-swings-are-more-frequent-than-in-2018 Published Time: 2026-10-10T05:43:00.798Z Markdown Content: Oct 10, 2026, 1:43 a.m. EDT 5 min read ![Image 1: BTC's 3-sigma days per year since 2016. (CoinDesk, TradingView)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2Fdd764207630edd2b441c0d7a7c060015ee0e6c90-1600x1060.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C80%2C1600%2C900%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=1200&q=75) BTC's 3-sigma days per year since 2016. (CoinDesk, TradingView) Samenvatting * Bitcoin has recorded 10 three-sigma trading days in 2026, exceeding the eight seen during the 2018 bear market, even as its annualized volatility has fallen to about 46% from 84%. * The frequency of extreme moves suggests that standard value-at-risk models, which rely heavily on recent volatility, may understate bitcoin’s tail risk and encourage overly large portfolio allocations. * Macroeconomic shocks and crowded derivatives trades can amplify sudden price swings, though deeper liquidity, stronger risk management and greater institutional participation have helped the market absorb them. Bitcoin [BTC$82.486,39](https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin) is experiencing more unusually large price swings this year than during the 2018 bear market, even as its overall volatility has fallen sharply, and that's a challenge for anyone relying on standard risk models. The largest cryptocurrency has recorded 10 days in 2026 when its price moved at least three standard deviations from its recent trading pattern, according to a CoinDesk analysis. That's more than the eight such days recorded during all of 2018, when bitcoin lost 73% of its value. The post has knocked the price of heating oil (diesel) for November delivery down by 1.6% to $4.66 per gallon.
